C4-01.title: They've taken the net
C4-01.scene: Both opponents came up to the net together. Your partner is at the back.
C4-01.cue: Both opponents are at the net, rackets up.
C4-01.question: What do you do?

answer.why: At the net, you're the target for two volleyers. Backing off gives you time to react.
answer.caption: You backed off and lobbed it back

lo.why: Backing off is right, but that's where volleys land at your feet.
lo.caption: You barely dig it out

hi.short: Hold your ground at the net
hi.why: One player can't block two volleyers. The spot right in front of them is the target.
hi.caption: Drilled at your feet

C4-01.coach: When they both come in, we both go back.
C4-01.next: When do you play two back?

C4-02.title: When to play two back
C4-02.scene: The opponent's serve is strong, and their net player keeps picking off our returns.
C4-02.cue: Three balls in a row came at your feet on the service line.
C4-02.question: Where do you stand this time?

answer.why: If the return floats off a big serve, the net player goes after you. With both back, you have time.
answer.caption: You held on from the back

lo.why: That's the standard spot, but right now the net player keeps aiming at your feet.
lo.caption: Another ball at your feet

hi.why: If the return floats, there's nowhere to hide up at the net.
hi.caption: Hit head-on

C4-02.coach: If you keep losing at the front, both go back.

C4-03.title: They're both up: the first-choice shot?
C4-03.scene: Both opponents are at the net, and you're both back.
C4-03.cue: The opponents are right up on the net.
C4-03.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: With both up close, the space over their heads is the biggest gap. Lob it down the middle and they leave it to each other.
answer.caption: Lobbed it over them

lo.why: A good second choice, but from the back it gets volleyed before it drops.
lo.caption: They volley it back

hi.why: Hit hard at two players at the net and it comes right back.
hi.caption: It came right back

C4-03.coach: When they're both at the net, the space over their heads is open.
C4-03.next: Which side do you lob to?

C4-04.title: Which side to lob?
C4-04.scene: Their net player is right up on the net, hunting our ball.
C4-04.cue: The back player is on the baseline, crosscourt.
C4-04.question: Where do you lob it?

answer.why: Lob over the net player and the back player has to run diagonally. Meanwhile we get set.
answer.caption: Lobbed it over the net player

lo.short: Crosscourt lob to the back player
lo.why: Safe, but the back player gets to hit it comfortably without moving.
lo.caption: They hit it back comfortably

hi.short: Short, in front of the net player
hi.why: A short lob feeds the net player's smash.
hi.caption: You got smashed

C4-04.coach: Lob over the net player — and deep.
C4-04.next: After the lob, do you move in?

C4-05.title: Move in right after the lob?
C4-05.scene: Your lob went over the net player and landed deep.
C4-05.cue: Both opponents turn and run back.
C4-05.question: What do you do?

answer.short: Move up to the service line
answer.why: The deep lob turned them around. Move in now to take back the net.
answer.caption: You took back the net

lo.why: Safe, but it gives them time to come back to the net.
lo.caption: They get set again

hi.short: Run all the way to the net
hi.why: If you keep running, a lob back goes over your head.
hi.caption: They lobbed it back

C4-05.coach: If the lob is deep, that's when you move forward.
C4-05.next: What if the lob was short?

C4-06.title: Your lob was short
C4-06.scene: Your lob is short. The opponent is waiting under it.
C4-06.cue: The opponent has the racket pulled back behind the head.
C4-06.question: How will the next ball come?

answer.why: A short lob is a smash chance. Get back, racket up, and get ready to return it.
answer.caption: You got it back up again

lo.why: It could, but off a short lob it usually comes hard. Move forward and you'll react late.
lo.caption: You got it back off your body

hi.why: There's no reason to send a short lob back high. Move in and you're right in front of the smash.
hi.caption: You were right in front of the smash

C4-06.coach: When your lob is short, expect the smash.
C4-06.next: Your stance right before the smash?

C4-07.title: Right before the smash
C4-07.scene: Your partner's lob was short, and a smash is coming from their left.
C4-07.cue: The smasher is on the left; you're back right.
C4-07.question: Where do you stand?

answer.short: A half step toward the middle
answer.why: A smash from the left usually goes down the middle or crosscourt. Stand inside that path.
answer.caption: You blocked it and lobbed again

lo.why: Not bad, but the middle between you is wide open.
lo.caption: You dove and got it

hi.why: Blocking a smash up close leaves you no time to react.
hi.caption: It came straight at you

C4-07.coach: Right before a smash, stay deep and get in its path.
C4-07.next: If you block it, where to?

C4-08.title: You blocked the smash — where to?
C4-08.scene: You barely got your racket on their smash from the back.
C4-08.cue: Both opponents are waiting at the net.
C4-08.question: Where do you send it?

answer.short: Lob it high and deep again
answer.why: A blocked ball has no pace. Lift it high and deep to get back in position.
answer.caption: You bought time

lo.why: It works if it's good, but it's hard to keep a block low.
lo.caption: They volleyed it back

hi.why: A short ball is a gift for two players at the net.
hi.caption: Finished at the net

C4-08.coach: Once you've blocked it, lob it high and start again.
C4-08.next: What if your partner gets pulled wide?

C4-09.title: Your partner got pulled off the court
C4-09.scene: An angle (short and wide) pulled your partner out wide to the left.
C4-09.cue: The middle of our court is empty.
C4-09.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: With your partner out wide, you take the middle. Move together, as if tied by a rope.
answer.caption: You covered the middle

lo.why: Guarding the right is right, but the middle is too far.
lo.caption: You barely reached it from afar

hi.why: Moving in while your partner is pushed back leaves the whole back middle open.
hi.caption: The back was open

C4-09.coach: When your partner is pulled out, you go to the middle.

C4-10.title: Covering: how far do you follow?
C4-10.scene: This time your partner got pulled way out wide right.
C4-10.cue: Their net player is at the net on the left.
C4-10.question: How far do you follow?

answer.why: Follow all the way and your side opens. Stop at the middle and you can reach both sides.
answer.caption: You reached both sides

lo.why: You hold your side, but you're late on a ball down the middle.
lo.caption: Late on the middle ball

hi.short: All the way to your partner's side
hi.why: If you both end up on the right, the whole left is open.
hi.caption: It went down the left

C4-10.coach: When you cover, go only as far as the middle.
C4-10.next: What if you're both pushed back?

C4-11.title: Low and fast — why not?
C4-11.scene: Their volley came deep and pushed you behind the baseline.
C4-11.cue: You're leaning back. Both opponents are at the net.
C4-11.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: From a pushed-back position, a low, fast ball hits the net. Lift it high to buy time.
answer.caption: You lifted it and held on

lo.short: Drop it slow down the middle
lo.why: It sometimes works, but it's hard to judge the length when you're pushed back.
lo.caption: Caught by a volley

hi.why: Hitting hard while leaning back keeps the ball low — into the net.
hi.caption: It went into the net

C4-11.coach: The more you're pushed, the higher and deeper.

C4-12.title: Aiming at their feet
C4-12.scene: Both opponents are at the net, and you can hit comfortably from the back.
C4-12.cue: Both opponents are two or three steps off the net.
C4-12.question: Where do you aim?

answer.short: Just over the net, at their feet
answer.why: Clear the net by a little and drop it at their feet. That forces them to lift it.
answer.caption: You finished the lifted ball

lo.why: A good idea, but at that height it gets volleyed before it passes.
lo.caption: Caught at waist height

hi.why: Chest height is the net player's favorite. It comes straight back.
hi.caption: It came straight back

C4-12.coach: To hit their feet, aim just over the net.

C4-13.title: The step from defense to attack
C4-13.scene: Your ball just cleared the net and landed at the opponent's feet.
C4-13.cue: The opponent gets the racket under it and lifts.
C4-13.question: Where do you hit it, and how?

answer.why: The moment they lift it is when defense turns to attack. Step in and volley the floater.
answer.caption: One step, and you attacked

lo.short: Let it bounce at the back
lo.why: Not bad, but while the floater bounces, they get set.
lo.caption: They got set

hi.why: A lifted ball drops short. Back off and the chance to attack is gone.
hi.caption: You missed the short ball

C4-13.coach: When they lift it, that's the moment to attack.

C4-14.title: You're both pushed out wide
C4-14.scene: Your partner is pushed out left; you're pushed out right.
C4-14.cue: The middle of our court is empty.
C4-14.question: How do you hang on?

answer.short: Lob high and come to the middle
answer.why: When you're both pushed out, lob high to buy time and both come back to the middle.
answer.caption: You both regrouped in the middle

lo.why: Hit hard and the ball comes back fast. Neither of you has time to get back.
lo.caption: Your partner barely blocks it

hi.short: Move forward and go for it
hi.why: Going for it while pushed out leaves the middle wide open.
hi.caption: It went through the middle

C4-14.coach: When you're both pushed out, lob high and regroup.
C4-14.next: What if you're pushed back twice in a row?

C4-15.title: No angle — the shot that keeps you alive
C4-15.scene: You've been chased out past the deep right corner.
C4-15.cue: One opponent is waiting at the net on the left.
C4-15.question: Where do you play to stay alive?

answer.why: From the corner, crosscourt is the longest path. Lift it high over the net player and deep.
answer.caption: You lifted it long and stayed alive

lo.why: It can keep you alive, but down the line is short and hard to judge.
lo.caption: Short, and you're pushed again

hi.short: Hard and low down the middle
hi.why: Hit hard from the corner and it goes to the net player's racket. That's the end.
hi.caption: The net player picked it off

C4-15.coach: From the corner, take the longest path — crosscourt.
C4-15.next: What if you're completely broken down?

C4-16.title: Take away their smash angle early
C4-16.scene: Your partner's lob is short. The opponent on the right is smashing.
C4-16.cue: You're at the net on the left; your partner is back right.
C4-16.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: A smash from the right usually goes to the middle and left. Back off into that path.
answer.caption: You blocked its path and lobbed it up

lo.why: Backing off is right, but the middle path is open.
lo.caption: You barely scooped it up

hi.why: Standing at the net in front of a short lob makes you the smash target.
hi.caption: The smash went in

C4-16.coach: Read the smash's path from the smasher's side.
C4-16.next: What if their smash is weak?

C4-17.title: Lob toward the weak smasher
C4-17.scene: The near net player has missed two smashes.
C4-17.cue: The crosscourt net player has a strong smash.
C4-17.question: Where do you lob it?

answer.short: Down the line over the near player
answer.why: Lob to the player who missed the smashes. Even down the line, over their head is safer.
answer.caption: Their smash went long

lo.short: A deep lob down the middle
lo.why: Not bad, but the strong smasher might take it.
lo.caption: They turn and get it

hi.why: Give a lob to the strong smasher and you'll get hit.
hi.caption: Hit by the strong smash

C4-17.coach: Lob to the side with the weaker smash.
C4-17.next: What about drawing them in with a short ball?

C4-18.title: Drawing them in with a short ball
C4-18.scene: Both opponents were back, so you drew them in with a short ball.
C4-18.cue: The opponent runs in and lifts the low ball.
C4-18.question: How will the next ball come?

answer.why: Running in to a short ball, they lift it. Take that ball up front.
answer.caption: Drew them in, then finished

lo.why: It could, but it's hard to hit deep while running in.
lo.caption: You just took the chance ball

hi.why: A lifted ball usually floats. Close in and it goes over your head.
hi.caption: It went over your head

C4-18.coach: Draw them in short, and the floater comes.
C4-18.next: What if you got drawn in?

C4-19.title: You came in for a short ball
C4-19.scene: You chased a short ball and got it back from the net.
C4-19.cue: Your partner is still back right.
C4-19.question: Where should you be?

answer.why: Now you're one-up, one-back. If the ball comes while you're running back, you can't play it.
answer.caption: You took it up front

lo.short: Back off to the service line only
lo.why: That's no man's land. The ball comes at your feet.
lo.caption: You took it at your feet

hi.why: A short ball drops behind you as you run back. If you came in, stay.
hi.caption: The front was open

C4-19.coach: If you got drawn in, stay at the net.

C4-20.title: Resetting after coming in
C4-20.scene: You came in for a short ball, and their net player is right in front of you.
C4-20.cue: The ball comes high — you have time.
C4-20.question: Where do you go after hitting?

answer.why: If it's hard to hold at the front, lob high to buy time and both go back.
answer.caption: You bought time and got back

lo.why: You can hang on, but right in front of their net player you stay a target.
lo.caption: You keep being the target

hi.why: A ball hit while backpedaling is short. Their net player drills it at your feet.
hi.caption: Drilled at your feet

C4-20.coach: When you came in and need to get back, lob high first.
C4-20.next: What if you're completely broken down?

C4-21.title: Completely broken down — your best shot
C4-21.scene: You've both lost your positions. Both opponents are at the net.
C4-21.cue: You're well behind the baseline; your partner is out to the left.
C4-21.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: When you're broken down, go as high as you can, down the middle. It gives them no angle and gives you both time.
answer.caption: You both got back

lo.why: Okay, but crosscourt still leaves an angle, so you get pushed once more.
lo.caption: Pushed one more time

hi.why: Hitting hard from a broken-down position hits the net or goes to the net player.
hi.caption: Caught by the net player

C4-21.coach: When you're broken down, go highest — down the middle.
C4-21.next: What if you're pushed back twice in a row?

C4-22.title: Pushed back twice in a row
C4-22.scene: You were pushed into the right corner twice in a row. You barely got a lob up.
C4-22.cue: The opponent at the net on the left raises the racket.
C4-22.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: When you're pushed again, get back to the middle first. Cutting the angle lets you survive the third ball.
answer.caption: You survived the third ball

lo.short: Stay out at the right edge
lo.why: From there the middle is too far. You barely get there.
lo.caption: You barely reach it from afar

hi.short: Move forward and go for it
hi.why: Moving forward after being pushed back puts you right in front of the smash.
hi.caption: Hit head-on

C4-22.coach: When you're pushed, recover first — then hang on.
C4-22.next: When do you switch to attack?

C4-23.title: The moment to switch from defense to attack
C4-23.scene: Off our deep lob, the opponent barely got it back from the corner.
C4-23.cue: The ball comes slow and high to the middle of our court.
C4-23.question: Where do you hit it, and how?

answer.short: Move in and hit it in the air
answer.why: Don't wait for a slow, high ball to bounce — move in and take it. That moment is your attack.
answer.caption: You finished it in the air

lo.why: Not bad, but while it bounces they get back in position.
lo.caption: They got back

hi.short: Back off and wait for a lob
hi.why: Waiting on a ball you should attack throws away the chance. It drops into the open front.
hi.caption: It dropped in the open front

C4-23.coach: Slow and high? That's when you attack.

C4-24.title: Chapter 4 review
C4-24.scene: Your partner's lob went over the net player and landed deep.
C4-24.cue: The opponent turns their back and chases the ball.
C4-24.question: How will the next ball come?

answer.why: A ball hit with their back to the net is high and weak. Move up and wait.
answer.caption: You moved in and took it

lo.why: It could, but it's hard to hit deep while chasing.
lo.caption: You got an ordinary ball

hi.why: Someone chasing it down can't hit hard. Back off and the weak ball drops in front of you.
hi.caption: You missed the weak ball

C4-24.coach: When they turn their back, we move forward.
